title_en: Guiding Case No. 219: Guangzhou Tianmou High-Tech New Materials Co., Ltd. and Jiujiang Tianmou High-Tech New Materials Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Niumou Fine Chemical Co., Ltd. et al. — dispute over infringement of technical secrets
ruling_gist_en:
1. When determining whether an act of intellectual property infringement constitutes a serious circumstance and whether punitive damages should be applied, comprehensive consideration may be given to factors such as whether the alleged infringer takes infringement of intellectual property as its business, whether it has been subject to criminal or administrative penalties, whether it constitutes repeat infringement, whether there is conduct obstructing the production of evidence in litigation, as well as the losses caused by the infringement or the amount of profits derived from the infringement, the scale of infringement, and the duration of the infringement.

2. Where an actor clearly knows that its conduct constitutes infringement, has actually carried out the infringing conduct, and such conduct constitutes its main business, it may be determined as taking infringement of intellectual property as its business. For those who take infringement of intellectual property as their business and engage in long-term, large-scale infringement, a multiplier for punitive damages may be applied from a higher end or even the maximum statutory multiplier in determining the amount of damages.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. 219

Guangzhou Tianmou Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. and Jiujiang Tianmou Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Niumou Fine Chemical Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over infringement of technical secrets

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 15, 2023)

Keywords

Civil; Infringement of technical secrets; Engaging in infringement of intellectual property rights as a business; Punitive damages; Amount of damages

Ruling Gist

1. In determining whether an act of infringement of intellectual property rights constitutes a serious circumstance and whether punitive damages are applicable, factors such as whether the alleged infringer engages in infringement as a business, whether it has been subject to criminal or administrative penalties, whether it constitutes repeated infringement, whether there is evidence obstruction in the litigation, as well as the losses caused by the infringement or the amount of profits gained from the infringement, the scale of infringement, and the duration of the infringement may be comprehensively considered.

2. Where a person, knowing that their conduct constitutes infringement, has actually carried out the infringing act and such act constitutes their main business, it may be determined that they engage in infringement as a business. For those who engage in infringement as a business and carry out long-term, large-scale infringing acts, the multiple of punitive damages may be applied at a high or even the maximum level in determining the amount of damages.

Basic Facts

On June 6, 2000, Guangzhou Tianmou Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Tianmou Company) was registered and established. On October 30, 2007, Jiujiang Tianmou Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jiujiang Tianmou Company) was registered and established, with Guangzhou Tianmou Company as its sole shareholder. To prove the licensing relationship regarding Carbomer technology between them, the two Tianmou Companies submitted two letters of authorization. The first letter of authorization, issued on September 30, 2008, stated: The production technology and intellectual property rights of Carbomer products independently developed by Guangzhou Tianmou Company are hereby granted to Jiujiang Tianmou Company for free use, with an authorization period of ten years from October 1, 2008 to September 30, 2018. During the authorization period, Jiujiang Tianmou Company has the right to use the technology, including but not limited to: using the technology to produce, manufacture, and sell products, using the technology to improve its current industrial processes, and making subsequent improvements to the technological achievements to form new technological achievements. Without the written consent and confirmation of both parties, Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company shall not grant the technology to any other unit or individual for use. After the authorization period expires, the granted right to use shall revert to Guangzhou Tianmou Company. The second letter of authorization, issued on September 15, 2018, has an authorization period from October 1, 2018 to September 30, 2028, with the same content as the first. The product involved in this case is Carbomer, also known as Carbomer (Chinese alias: polyacrylic acid, carboxyvinyl copolymer). Neutralized Carbomer is an excellent gel matrix, widely used in emulsions, creams, and gels.

On August 29, 2011, Anhui Niumou Fine Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Anhui Niumou Company) was registered and established. At the time of its establishment, the legal representative was Liu Mou, with Liu Mou holding a 70% capital contribution. The legal representative was later changed to Wu Moucheng.

Hua Mou joined Guangzhou Tianmou Company on March 30, 2004, and resigned on November 8, 2013. From December 30, 2007, until his resignation, Hua Mou signed documents such as the "Labor Contract," "Commercial Confidentiality and Non-Competition Agreement," "Employee Handbook," and "Special Training Agreement" with Guangzhou Tianmou Company, which provided for confidentiality obligations regarding trade secrets and non-competition restrictions. Zhu Mouliang and Hu Mouchun had previously worked at Guangzhou Tianmou Company and signed the "Labor Contract," "Commercial Confidentiality and Non-Competition Agreement," and "Commercial Technology Confidentiality Agreement" with Guangzhou Tianmou Company during their employment. Between 2012 and 2013, Hua Mou, using his position as the head of Carbomer product research and development, obtained the equipment drawings of the reactor and dryer for the Carbomer production process technology from Li Moumou, the production workshop director of Jiujiang Tianmou Company, under the pretext of writing a thesis. He also repeatedly copied information on the process equipment of the Carbomer production project from his office computer at Guangzhou Tianmou Company to external storage media, violating Guangzhou Tianmou Company's management system. After illegally obtaining the production process materials of the Carbomer technology from the two Tianmou Companies, Hua Mou sent the original drawings and documents of the Carbomer production process of the two Tianmou Companies to Liu Mou, Zhu Mouliang, Hu Mouchun, and others via USB drive copying or email. Hua Mou, Liu Mou, Zhu Mouliang, and Hu Mouchun discussed the use of the original drawings of the Carbomer production process technology of the two Tianmou Companies. During this process, both Hu Mouchun and Zhu Mouliang raised the question of whether it would infringe the relevant rights of Jiujiang Tianmou Company. Hua Mou then instructed Hu Mouchun to design Anhui Niumou Company's production process based on the original drawings of the Carbomer production process technology of the two Tianmou Companies, and told Hu Mouchun not to make it exactly the same as that of the two Tianmou Companies during the design. Accordingly, Hu Mouchun modified the Carbomer process design drawings of Guangzhou Tianmou Company according to Hua Mou's instructions, and finally entrusted the modified drawings to the Hefei Branch of a certain Shandong Engineering Design Co., Ltd. for design, commissioned a certain Jiangsu Machinery Manufacturing Co., Ltd. to manufacture the reactor, ordered the same crushing machinery equipment as that used by the two Tianmou Companies from a certain Shanghai Powder Machinery Manufacturing Company that had a cooperative relationship with the two Tianmou Companies, and then commissioned a certain Wuxi, Jiangsu Mixing Equipment Co., Ltd. to design the assembly drawing based on the technical solution of a certain Jiangsu Mechanical Co., Ltd., and then produced the mixer according to the assembly drawing.

At least from 2014, Anhui Niumou Company used the Carbomer production process and equipment technology illegally obtained by Hua Mou from the two Tianmou Companies to produce Carbomer products and sell them to domestic and foreign companies, with sales covering more than 20 countries and regions. Producing Carbomer products was the main business of Anhui Niumou Company, and there was no evidence that it produced any other products. In January 2018, Liu Mou, the former legal representative of Anhui Niumou Company, and others were held criminally liable for the crime of infringing trade secrets. Even after the relevant criminal judgment had determined that Hua Mou, Liu Mou, and others had committed acts of infringing the trade secrets of the rights holder, Anhui Niumou Company still did not stop the infringement. Based on the relevant evidence, Anhui Niumou Company continuously sold Carbomer products from 2014 until August 2019.

Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company filed a lawsuit in 2017 against Anhui Niumou Company, Hua Mou, Liu Mou, Hu Mouchun, Zhu Mouliang, and others on the grounds that they had infringed their Carbomer technical secrets, requesting the court to order the defendants to cease the infringement, compensate for losses, and make an apology.

Judgment

The Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court rendered civil judgment (2017) Yue 73 Min Chu No. 2163 on July 19, 2019: 1. Hua Mou, Liu Mou, Hu Mouchun, Zhu Mouliang, and Anhui Niumou Company shall immediately cease infringing the technical secrets involved in the case of Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company upon the effectiveness of this judgment, and destroy the process materials containing the technical secrets involved in the case. 2. Anhui Niumou Company shall pay Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company economic losses of RMB 30 million and reasonable expenses of RMB 400,000 within ten days of the effectiveness of this judgment. Hua Mou, Liu Mou, Hu Mouchun, and Zhu Mouliang shall bear joint and several liability for the aforementioned compensation amounts within the ranges of RMB 5 million, RMB 5 million, RMB 1 million, and RMB 1 million, respectively. 3. Other claims of Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company are dismissed. After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, Guangzhou Tianmou Company, Jiujiang Tianmou Company, Anhui Niumou Company, Hua Mou, and Liu Mou appealed to the Supreme People's Court.

The Supreme People's Court rendered civil judgment (2019) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 562 on November 24, 2020: 1. The first and third items of the civil judgment (2017) Yue 73 Min Chu No. 2163 of the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court are affirmed. 2. The second item of the civil judgment (2017) Yue 73 Min Chu No. 2163 of the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court is modified to: Anhui Niumou Company shall pay Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company economic losses of RMB 30 million and reasonable expenses of RMB 400,000 within ten days of the effectiveness of this judgment. Hua Mou, Liu Mou, Hu Mouchun, and Zhu Mouliang shall bear joint and several liability for the aforementioned compensation amounts within the ranges of RMB 5 million, RMB 30 million, RMB 1 million, and RMB 1 million, respectively. 3. Other appeal requests of Guangzhou Tianmou Company and Jiujiang Tianmou Company are dismissed. 4. The appeal requests of Hua Mou, Liu Mou, and Anhui Niumou Company are dismissed. After the second-instance judgment was pronounced, Anhui Niumou Company, Hua Mou, and Liu Mou applied to the Supreme People's Court for retrial.

The Supreme People's Court rendered civil ruling (2021) Zui Gao Fa Min Shen No. 4025 on October 12, 2021: The retrial applications of Hua Mou, Liu Mou, and Anhui Niumou Company are dismissed.

Reasoning

The Supreme People's Court held: Article 17, Paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Anti-Unfair Competition Law) provides that the amount of compensation for an operator harmed by an act of unfair competition shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the operator due to the infringement; if the actual losses are difficult to calculate, it shall be determined based on the profits gained by the infringer from the infringement. Where an operator maliciously commits an act of infringing trade secrets, and the circumstances are serious, the amount of compensation may be determined at one to five times the amount determined according to the above methods. The amount of compensation shall also include the reasonable expenses incurred by the operator to stop the infringement.

In this case, the actual losses of the two Tianmou Companies could not be determined. Therefore, the infringement profits of Anhui Niumou Company were calculated based on the verified partial sales situation of Anhui Niumou Company. The Carbomer products produced by Anhui Niumou Company, their processes, procedures, and some equipment infringed the technical secrets involved in the case of the two Tianmou Companies, but its Carbomer formula was not found to infringe the technical secrets of the two Tianmou Companies. When determining the infringement profits, the court of first instance did not consider the role of the technical secrets involved in the case in the production of Carbomer, nor did it fully consider the role of other production factors apart from the technical secret information in the production process of Carbomer products. By multiplying the sales amount of over RMB 37 million self-admitted by Anhui Niumou Company by the gross profit margin of the fine chemical industry of 32.26%, the verifiable partial infringement profits of Anhui Niumou Company were approximately RMB 12 million. Now, comprehensively considering the role played by the infringed technical secrets involved in the case in the production process of Carbomer products, the contribution degree of the technical secrets involved is determined to be 50% at discretion. Therefore, the infringement profits of Anhui Niumou Company are correspondingly reduced to an integer of RMB 6 million. Regarding the choice of profit rate, since Anhui Niumou Company did not provide original accounting vouchers, account books, or profit statements as required by the court, nor did it adduce evidence to prove the profit rate of its Carbomer products, it should bear the legal consequences of failing to adduce evidence. Therefore, the product profit rate is determined based on the gross profit margin of the fine chemical industry published in the annual report of Guangzhou Tianmou Company.

Although Anhui Niumou Company submitted evidence such as its business license to the court in the second instance to show that its business scope included more than just Carbomer products, based on the established facts, Anhui Niumou Company did not produce any other products besides Carbomer products, nor did Anhui Niumou Company further adduce evidence to prove that it produced other products besides Carbomer products. In this case, the infringing act of Hua Mou disclosing technical secrets occurred between 2012 and 2013. Anhui Niumou Company used the Carbomer production process and equipment technology illegally obtained by Hua Mou from the two Tianmou Companies to produce Carbomer products and sell them domestically and abroad. Furthermore, Anhui Niumou Company explicitly stated that all Carbomer products it produced were made with the same equipment. Whether a person engages in infringement as a business can be determined from both subjective and objective aspects. Objectively, the person has actually carried out the infringing act, and it constitutes the company's main business and main source of profit; subjectively, the person, including the company's actual controller and management, knows that their conduct constitutes infringement but still carries it out. The conduct of Anhui Niumou Company and Liu Mou in this case falls under such circumstances.

Article 17, Paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law stipulates the conditions for imposing punitive damages and the range of multiples for punitive damages. It can be seen that if an operator maliciously infringes on another's trade secrets and the circumstances are serious, the right holder may request the infringer to bear punitive damages at a corresponding multiple of the compensation amount. Therefore, in this case, whether punitive damages are applicable should be determined based on whether Anhui Niumou Company engaged in malicious infringement and whether the circumstances were serious. According to the facts established in this case, since its establishment, Anhui Niumou Company's business has been the production of Carbomer products. Although it argued that it also produced other products, it did not submit evidence to support this. Moreover, although the names of the Carbomer products it produced varied, they were all processed by the same set of equipment. In addition, after its former legal representative, Liu Mou, was held criminally liable for the crime of infringing trade secrets and was found to have committed acts of infringing the trade secrets of the right holder, Anhui Niumou Company still did not stop production, and its sales covered more than 20 countries and regions. At the same time, during the original trial of this case, it refused to provide relevant accounting books and original vouchers without justifiable reasons, constituting obstruction of evidence. This fully demonstrates the depth of its subjective intent to infringe and the seriousness of the infringement circumstances. Given that the alleged infringing acts in this case spanned before and after the amendment and implementation of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law on April 23, 2019, and that Anhui Niumou Company's refusal to provide financial books and other materials constituted obstruction of evidence, the determined infringement profits were based on the sales volume self-admitted by Anhui Niumou Company, which was only part of its infringement profits. The infringer did not submit evidence in this case to prove its specific profits before and after the amendment of the law, making it impossible to calculate the compensation in segments with April 23, 2019 as the boundary. Existing evidence shows that Anhui Niumou Company did not stop its infringing acts after the first-instance judgment; its acts were continuous, with a huge scale and long duration of infringement. As a result, it is objectively difficult to calculate the compensation amount in segments based on the evidence on file. The original intention of establishing the punitive damages system in the Anti-Unfair Competition Law is to enhance legal deterrence, combat malicious and serious infringement, deter and discourage future or potential infringers, effectively protect innovation activities, and impose heavier penalties on long-term malicious infringements. Therefore, in this case, the amount of damages for this case can be determined at a high level based on the determined infringement profits of Anhui Niumou Company.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 17, Paragraph 3 of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended on April 23, 2019)
